Governing sources are docs/scope.md T8 and Working rules, docs/vision.md (test volume is not confidence; Linux is headless CI), docs/invariants.md, AGENTS.md's local harness/GPU contracts, the epic, original children hud-bstmy.1.1-.1.5, gen-1 hud-bstmy.1.6, corrections hud-bstmy.1.7-.1.10, and any later enabler children such as hud-bstmy.1.12. All original criteria remain audit obligations. The broader T8 resource tests/code diet/reference removal belong to their existing sibling epics; record their relationship without implementing or absorbing them into this enabler audit.

Non-goals: No Rust, Python, workflow, recipe, manifest, spec, or product documentation edits; no new tests, production serialization policy, CI/ruleset changes, issue creation/update/close/dependency mutation, or owner decision. The coordinator owns all Beads lifecycle and materializes follow-ups. Do not restore pre-reset RFC/OpenSpec/doctrine requirements. Do not wait for unanswered needs-human escalations whose documented default is status quo.

Bootstrap and sequencing: Work in the assigned isolated worktree and expected agent branch; verify actual shell cwd, canonical common Git directory, and absence of repository-identity Git environment overrides. Record HEAD before reading or running checks; re-grep sources because old line numbers are historical. Read AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, then compact current parent/sibling fields and dependency state. hud-bstmy.1.7-.1.10 are existing prerequisites; a closed child is an evidence lead, not a coverage verdict. If .1.12 is still open, report the residual serialization finding against that existing bead and allow the coordinator to wire/sequence it; never create a duplicate or silently declare full coverage.

Owned audit map and required rows:
A. GPU local signal (.1.1, .1.8, and later .1.12): inspect justfile's actual ICD discovery and every GPU-building recipe, compositor renderer/tests/mod.rs, renderer/tests/surface.rs, compositor tests/common/mod.rs and every compositor test binary, runtime src/test_support.rs, runtime tests/pixel_helpers.rs, present_ack.rs, tests/integration, examples/vertical_slice, and canonical app boot tests. Verify one shared async serialization gate per multi-test binary, its protected operation and lifetime, and any single-GPU-test exception by proving no competing creation path exists in that binary. Distinguish construction-only helpers from runtime-lib guards held across an entire scenario, and per-process locks from cross-process coordination. Do not assume HEADLESS_FORCE_SOFTWARE excludes a hardware Vulkan ICD. Enumerate every GPU recipe, including test, test-gpu, test-integration, both token-footprint runs, production-boot and canonical-app-boot, plus newly discovered recipes. Compare their environment and target/feature flags against CI. ICD discovery must follow justfile's actual lvp selection, supporting both lvp_icd.x86_64.json and Mesa 25's lvp_icd.json; dry-runs in this baseline select lvp_icd.json.
B. Local/CI parity (.1.2, .1.9, .1.10): inspect every run step in .github/workflows/ci.yml and just --dry-run ci. Map validation commands/targets/features/environment to recipes; explicitly classify platform provisioning, artifact upload, informational duplicate pixel-readback, and weekly performance exclusions rather than pretending they are local behavior gates. C. D. If an explicit answer exists, include the resulting implementation bead and actual delivered follow-up in the matrix, verify the stated ruleset coordination through read-only evidence, and report unresolved coordination to the coordinator. Audit method: For every universal or negative claim, save the complete searched surface and constructor/recipe/package/test inventory, then assess every entry. Audit guard instruments themselves: feature traversal, target/package exclusions, GPU skip/canary behavior, discovery roots, unittest enumeration and every source-scan regex/glob/root used as evidence. Each scenario needs one adequate gate species: an existing behavior-executing test or the designated structural scan/type/lint rule. A passing but blind guard is a gap in that guard, not justification for another redundant test.

Behavior and verification matrix: Happy path is complete traced coverage plus clean real metadata and executed representative GPU/CI gates. Invalid metadata or missing shipped package must fail the guard, while legitimate dev-only/test-only and inactive optional edges must retain the documented behavior. Concurrency evidence covers all in-process initialization sites and guard release on failure; do not equate software-adapter selection with serialization. Missing tools, adapter, ICD, skipped tests, timeouts and failed commands are recorded as unverified/failed, never implemented-by-green-skip. Replay/idempotence means reruns on the same SHA preserve classification and token-footprint measurements, with no new mutation or duplicate gap candidates. Concurrent main changes require a fresh source re-grep and a new evidence SHA; mixed-SHA evidence is invalid. Cancellation leaves an incomplete report whose unexecuted commands are explicit. Rollback and persistent-schema migration are not applicable because this audit changes no production or stored state. Historical split compatibility and named invariant retention remain applicable.

Run just ci once for the integrated parity proof; its fmt/clippy/check/test/boot contracts remain obligations, and any tool-gated SKIP is explicitly an evidence limitation. Prefer existing valid exact-SHA evidence over blindly re-running unrelated expensive suites, but never substitute old-commit evidence for a changed surface. Documentation impact: No direct documentation/spec amendment is authorized in this READ-ONLY bead. The report must include file:line proposals for any stale README/AGENTS/CLAUDE/justfile/CI/invariants statements, with the governing source and exact discrepancy. Investigation notes belong in the coordinator handoff or subsequent PR description, not new docs investigation files, per docs/scope.md Working rules. hud-lirh2.8.title: T7: runtime PortalDriver with injected time and safe-mode pause
hud-lirh2.8.description:
Goal: fold the driver into crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/portal.rs (~750 prod lines), use the scene clock (invariant 9), mirror hub transitions onto the scene lease, and pause portal liveness during safe mode.

Why: the driver reads SystemTime (now_wall_us(), driver:2739) while the lease uses the scene clock; portal liveness keeps running in safe mode, so held-off agents get reaped right after resume (conflicts with invariant 5; behavior fix -- flag in the PR).
Non-goals: windowed/portal.rs dedup (next bead).
Governing spec: docs/invariants.md §4, §5, §9; docs/scope.md 'Tranches' T7 row; docs/api.md 'MCP tools' portal verbs and 'Errors'; docs/invariants.md §2-§5, §8, §9. Line refs are at windows-release-pipeline@44d355ef (content identical to main@1eb8f7cb, the merge of PR #1245); re-grep symbols before editing. The planning survey that produced this bead is not persisted; everything needed is in this bead.
hud-lirh2.8.design:
Rename portal_projection_driver.rs -> portal.rs. PortalDriver owns HashMap<PortalKey, Binding{tile, lease, prev_content_height_px, surface_declared}> + tokens; drain(&hub, &mut scene, &mut input, now): (1) lock hub: sweep + take_due, unlock; (2) transitions: Degraded -> disconnect_lease (orphan badge, invariant 4), Recovered -> reconnect_lease, Reclaim -> revoke_lease + tile delete; (3) due views: ensure tile+lease at first render (default geometry), render, apply; (4) follow-tail/head-trim notifications to InputProcessor; (5) terminal leases (dismiss) -> hub.remove(key). Replace now_wall_us() with scene.now_wall_us(). Lease handling = grant-on-create + mirror (shrink ensure_projection_lease driver:2530). Remove pending_tile_removals/pending_lease_revocations deferral. next_wake_deadline = min(hub.next_deadline, lease deadlines) (six PortalDeadlineFamily values -> two). Safe mode enter/exit (shell/safe_mode.rs, entry wired by the POC hotkey bead) calls hub.suspend_clock/resume_clock. Dismiss path from the POC viewer-dismiss bead becomes the terminal-lease -> hub.remove path; dismissed portal re-attaches fresh on next publish.
Tests: keep/rename portal_degrade_then_publish_within_grace_resumes_same_tile (was disconnect_then_reconnect_within_grace_resumes_same_surface_without_duplication; update invariants.md §4); reclaimed_portal_removes_tile_and_state (was disconnected_portal_surface_removed_on_grace_expiry_yields_no_further_state); keep terminal_resident_lease_reconciles_without_past_deadline_spin, partial_agent_liveness_recovery_reaps_only_the_stale_projection, parked_portal_repaints_pending_count_at_input_expiry; add portal_liveness_paused_during_safe_mode (invariants.md §5) and dismissed_portal_reattaches_fresh_on_next_publish (§3). Target ~1.1k test lines.
Run strictly serially with the other T7 beads (portal files collide heavily, AGENTS.md); branch from current main. The token_footprint gate is byte-exact (check_token_footprint.py fingerprints request/response bodies); bodies must stay identical.

hud-zrs6.title: Shell #2: Safe mode — suspend and resume
hud-zrs6.description:
# Safe Mode: Suspend and Resume

Implement the safe mode protocol that suspends all agent leases (not revoke — identity preserved), renders a safe mode overlay, and restores leases on explicit viewer exit.

## Ownership rule
The shell is the SOLE owner of safe mode state transitions. Policy-arbitration evaluates triggers (Level 0 Human Override, Level 1 Safety) but does NOT transition shell state. Only the shell state machine writes OverrideState.safe_mode. The shell is also the sole writer of OverrideState.freeze_active — safe mode entry cancels any active freeze.

## Spec references (system-shell/spec.md)

### Requirement: Safe Mode Entry Protocol (line 89)
Safe mode enterable by: (1) Ctrl+Shift+Escape or "Dismiss All" chrome control (Level 0 Human Override), (2) automatic on critical runtime error (GPU device loss, scene graph corruption, unrecoverable render failure — Level 1 Safety). On entry: all active leases suspended (NOT revoked), all agent sessions receive SessionSuspended with reason safe_mode, safe mode overlay rendered, all input captured by chrome layer.
- Scenario: Manual safe mode entry (line 94) — WHEN viewer presses Ctrl+Shift+Escape THEN all active leases suspended, agents receive SessionSuspended, overlay appears, all input routes to chrome
- Scenario: Auto safe mode on GPU loss (line 98) — WHEN compositor detects wgpu::DeviceError::Lost THEN runtime enters safe mode with SafeModeEntryReason = CRITICAL_ERROR

### Requirement: Safe Mode Overlay (line 102)
Overlay displays: centered banner ("Safe Mode -- All agent sessions paused."), prominent "Resume" button, current viewer class indicator, no agent branding/content. Renders correctly even if scene graph corrupted (reads from ChromeState and theme colors/font atlas only).
- Scenario: Safe mode overlay rendering (line 107) — WHEN safe mode entered THEN full-viewport overlay with banner, Resume button, viewer class icon, no agent content
- Scenario: Overlay with corrupted scene graph (line 111) — WHEN safe mode entered due to scene graph corruption THEN overlay still renders correctly

### Requirement: Safe Mode Exit (line 115)
Exit only by explicit viewer action: click/tap "Resume", Enter/Space (resume button has focus by default), or Ctrl+Shift+Escape toggle. On exit: overlay dismissed, SUSPENDED leases transition to ACTIVE, sessions receive SessionResumed (empty message), each lease receives LeaseResume with adjusted_expires_at_wall_us and suspension_duration_us, TTL clocks resume with suspension time excluded, staleness badges clear within 1 frame, mutations accepted again, compositor resumes from current scene state. Agents do NOT re-request leases — identity, capability scope, and resource budget preserved across ACTIVE -> SUSPENDED -> ACTIVE cycle.
- Scenario: Resume from safe mode (line 120) — WHEN viewer clicks Resume THEN overlay dismissed, SUSPENDED leases to ACTIVE, SessionResumed sent, LeaseResume with adjusted expiry sent, staleness badges clear within 1 frame, mutations accepted without re-request

### Requirement: Safe Mode and Freeze Interaction (Shell State Invariant) (line 124)
State invariant: safe_mode=true implies freeze_active=false. The shell is the sole writer of OverrideState.freeze_active. On any safe mode activation: freeze cancelled, freeze queue discarded, freeze_active=false BEFORE any other safe mode entry steps. Freeze attempted during safe mode is ignored. After safe mode exit, freeze is inactive.
- Scenario: Safe mode cancels freeze (automatic trigger) (line 129) — WHEN scene frozen and GPU failure triggers safe mode THEN freeze cancelled, queue discarded, freeze_active=false, overlay appears
- Scenario: Safe mode cancels freeze (manual trigger) (line 133) — WHEN scene frozen and viewer triggers safe mode via Ctrl+Shift+Escape THEN freeze cancelled, queue discarded, freeze_active=false, overlay appears
- Scenario: Freeze ignored during safe mode (line 137) — WHEN viewer presses Ctrl+Shift+F while safe mode active THEN no effect; safe mode captures all input

## Secondary spec references

### lease-governance/spec.md
- Requirement: Safe Mode Suspends Leases (line 92) — all active leases transition to SUSPENDED on safe mode entry
- Requirement: Safe Mode Resume (line 105) — on exit, SUSPENDED leases transition to ACTIVE; SessionResumed and LeaseResume sent; resume within 2 frames (33.2ms)
- Requirement: Max Suspension Time (line 114) — maximum suspension duration before auto-resume
- Requirement: Suspension Preserves State (line 123) — lease identity/capabilities/budgets preserved

### policy-arbitration/spec.md
- Requirement: Level 0 Human Override (line 48) — policy evaluates Ctrl+Shift+Escape as Level 0 but the shell transitions state

## Acceptance criteria
- Safe mode suspends all active leases (SUSPENDED not REVOKED)
- SessionSuspended sent to all agent sessions with reason safe_mode
- Mutations rejected during safe mode
- Safe mode overlay renders correctly (banner, Resume button, viewer class, no agent content)
- Overlay renders correctly even with corrupted scene graph
- Exit via Resume/Enter/Space/Ctrl+Shift+Escape toggle restores leases to ACTIVE
- SessionResumed (empty) and LeaseResume (with adjusted TTL) sent on exit
- TTL pause verified: suspension time excluded from TTL accounting
- Staleness badges clear within 1 frame of resume
- Freeze cancelled on safe mode entry (freeze_active=false before other steps)
- Freeze queue discarded on safe mode entry
- Freeze attempt during safe mode ignored
- After safe mode exit, freeze is inactive
- Resume completes within 2 frames (33.2ms)
- Test scenes: policy_matrix_basic (safe mode overrides all policy levels)

## v1-mandatory requirements
- Safe Mode Entry Protocol (line 89)
- Safe Mode Overlay (line 102)
- Safe Mode Exit (line 115)
- Safe Mode and Freeze Interaction (Shell State Invariant) (line 124)

## v1-reserved exclusions
None for this bead.

## post-v1 exclusions
None for this bead.

## Crate/file location
crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/shell/safe_mode.rs — safe mode state machine, entry/exit logic, overlay rendering, freeze cancellation on entry

## What this does NOT include
- Chrome layer rendering (bead #1)
- Freeze queue implementation (bead #3)
- Privacy redaction (bead #4)
- Disconnection badges (bead #5)
- Lease state machine implementation (Epic 4)
- Policy evaluation logic (Epic 8)
